Living in a frat house had its benefits, it was cheap, and for a financially struggling college student it… it was cheap.

It had a hell of a lot more drawbacks, in Phainon’s opinion. The smell of sweat and booze that just seemed to linger no matter how many times he scrubbed the kitchen, the discarded beer cans and bottles that nobody ever bothers to take out on recycling day, but most egregious of all must be the lack of privacy.

Phainon had returned home after a long day of assignments only to find that the door to his room had been locked from the inside.

And somebody was making noises, from inside his own room.

Very suggestive ones, for that matter.

“Wow, I thought those kinds of things only happened in movies. Your frat brothers are… interesting.” When his life is falling apart, at least he can always count on his dear friend Mydei to lend a listening ear to his moans. Nevermind, wrong choice of wording, the trauma from what he overheard is still fresh in his mind.

Beautiful, sweet, perfect Mydei, who despite his grumbling was kind enough to come and hang out in the arcade at ass o’clock on a weekday. The blonde man drops a coin into the machine slot and picks the same character he always uses, the muscled berserker type that the internet claims is hard to play, but Mydei makes it work somehow.

“Interesting?” Phainon repeats in disbelief, buttons clacking as he wastes time choosing his character until he decides on the hero, sword of light and all. “I wish I knew how to wipe my own memory.”.

The game begins, Mydei and Phainon both fall silent as their fingers dance around the controller buttons, trying to get the upper hand on each other. Mydei has a more aggressive approach, he always does. Phainon knows him well enough that the best strategy is to focus on dodges and blocks until he gets his chance to counterattack.

“I wish I could move out, but my lease lasts until the end of term,” Phainon sighs. He finally lands a combo and Mydei’s character stumbles back, health bar sliced nearly in half.

“You voluntarily signed the lease, you just have to deal with it until it’s up,” Mydei replies heartlessly, eyes fixed on the screen. With a few button presses he unleashes his character’s ultimate and red crystals fill the screen, shearing Phainon’s health until it’s almost nothing.

“You’re always so mean to me, Mydei,” Phainon whines, referring to both his comment and the sudden attack that almost kills his character. But Phainon plays better when he’s under pressure. His fingers move lightning fast, blocking and evading at just the right moments, well-timed attacks cleaving away at Mydei’s health bar.

“I want to find love too,” Phainon suddenly says. His voice is muffled by the sounds of the arcade, but Mydei hears it loud and clear.

Mydei falters, his grip on the joystick slipping, missing his cue to counterattack, just a heartbeat too slow. Phainon takes the opportunity to unleash another devastating combo, quick and merciless. Mydei’s health drops even more, his blocks ineffectual under Phainon’s barrage until the screen explodes into a bright red ‘K.O.’

“That came out of nowhere.” Mydei says. Tickets trail out of the machine, pooling around their shoes. But Mydei is looking straight at Phainon, gold eyes focusing only on him.

“We’re almost into our third and final year and I still haven’t experienced the whirlwind college romance I was promised!”

Mydei just raises an eyebrow at him. “The girls in the history department call you the ‘Snowy Prince’. I thought you of all people would have no shortage of admirers.”

Phainon snorts. It’s not like Phainon hasn’t been asked out before. He’s popular, friendly, athletic and one of the top students in the law department. Not to be full of himself, but his looks are nothing to scoff at either, all the aunties back home can’t stop cooing over how handsome he is.

But still, none of those people had stirred his heart, not even a little bit.

Trying to change the subject, Phainon says with a smirk. “You’d be surprised, but, not really. Besides, if anyone deserves the title of ‘Prince’, it should be you, right, Mydei?”

Mydei doesn’t dignify that with a response, instead giving Phainon the familiar withering look reserved for when he’s saying something stupid.

But titans, Mydei looks devastatingly good underneath the flickering, pulsating lights of the arcade. The glow of neon red and electric blue ripples across his skin, casting shadows over his sharp, red tattoos. He crosses his arms, muscles bulging and fully visible due to his choice of a red sleeveless shirt. His hair turns technicolor in the light, blonde darkening to red at the tips like blood. The arcade is stuffy, skimping on air conditioning, and the locks of hair stick slightly to his nape as he shifts.

“I’m serious!” Phainon insists, never one to back down in a competition with Mydei, even if it is entirely self-imposed and one-sided. “I mean like… look at you! You’re kind, well-read, soft-spoken, and your body is so conspicuous that even I’m jealous of it. You’re totally prince material.”

Mydei leans back, resting his elbows against the machine, the furrow between his eyebrows deepening. “I often think this, but there’s something wrong with your brain.”

To Phainon, that’s as good as an admission, a victory.

It’s not like he doesn’t mean it. Although Phainon perhaps has the more typical characteristics of a prince, blue eyes, white hair, a charming smile that could get him almost anything he wants, Mydei is one among them who truly embodies princely qualities. He’s the only person Phainon knows who is the definition of ‘beautiful’, ‘handsome’, and ‘hot’ all in one package. Despite his full body tattoos and the permanent scowl on his face, he has a classical beauty that people would write poems about.

Get to know Mydei a little more, and one will realize he’s perfect on the inside too. Loves reading, a good cook, thoughtful and observant, skilled at playing the guitar, with an indomitable personality that never seems to falter to matter the circumstances.

Phainon is envious of him in that regard too, as he still finds himself full of insecurities and the latest one seems to be his inability to find a romantic partner.

“Mydei, I have a request, be my dating coach!” He practically leans over to Mydei’s side, taking both of Mydei’s hands in his.

Perhaps it’s the dim lighting of the arcade, but Mydei’s face seems to flush red. “HKS! What nonsense are you talking about?”

“Pleasseeee Mydei! Help me out! I really want to start dating!” Phainon begs, using his best ‘kicked puppy’ expression that he knows Mydei is weak to.

“Grown ass man,” Mydei grumbles under his breath, but the way he’s not making eye contact with Phainon lets him know that it’s only seconds before he concedes. And right on cue, Mydei sighs.

“Has there really been nobody who catches your eye over the last 2 years?” Mydei asks quietly.  Is it a trick of the light or was there… hesitance in those golden eyes?

Phainon squints at him, trying to figure him out. But it’s not like Mydei to be obtuse, the man had always been straightforward, sometimes to an infuriating degree. With Mydei, you can always be sure he only says what he means, so Phainon doesn’t think too much about it when he shakes his head.

“No.”

“Nobody at all?” Mydei asks again.

“Really, there’s been nobody,” Phainon says. When every potential partner inadvertently gets compared to Mydei, they’re all bound to fall short.

“I see…” Mydei mutters quietly, something unreadable flashing over those fierce, feline-like eyes before it disappears again. “And why would you even ask me? It’s not like I’ve been in a relationship either.”

Mydei puts his hands on the controller again, seemingly losing interest in their conversation. “Come on, let’s play again. I’ll be victorious this time.”

That is true, ever since Phainon first met Mydei in their first year, they had both been single. And even if Mydei hadn’t told him, he doubted that his friend had been in a relationship before, because he doubted there was anyone idiotic enough to break up with Mydeimos. Besides, Mydei shouldn’t be settling for just anyone, any potential partner would have to be as impressive as him, at the very least.

As Phainon thinks that, something that feels like envy makes his stomach churn and bile rise to his throat. Why is that? He is certainly not that shallow to be bitter at the idea of Mydei getting into a relationship before himself. And he is definitely not that competitive… At least, he hopes he isn’t.

Phainon starts as the screen flashes with the large red ‘K.O’. Despite having a strong start he seemed to have lost again.

“That makes it 7:3, seven for me, three for you.” It was stated matter-of-factly, Mydei had stopped gloating two rounds ago, which means that Phainon must be in really bad shape.

“You look unwell.” Phainon jerks up with a guilty start. Mydei is still in the same relaxed pose, arms draped over the sides of the machine. But his eyes are sharp, molten gold tracking Phainon with the intensity of someone used to reading people closely, quietly. “Is a small matter truly bothering you that much?”

“No it’s- it’s not that,” Phainon says, suddenly very interested in the ‘GAME OVER-RESTART? ’ screen. “I was just thinking.”

“Don’t strain yourself.” Mydei says dryly. “Tell me what idiotic thoughts are brewing in your head this time.”

Phainon chuckles, it comes out pretty forced. He runs a hand through his hair, messy and slightly greasy from a full day out and about. He wishes he could just go home, shower, and crawl into bed, like what he wanted to do initially before this all happened. “I just thought that I’d be kind of sad if you fell in love before me.”

Mydei exhales deeply, rubbing the bridge of his nose like he’s bracing for a headache.

“How would I even help you?” Even though he has made it clear how abhorrent he finds the idea, Mydei is still not saying no. Phainon could almost cry at how nice he’s being.

“It’s easy, you just need to give me your brutally honest advice on what I’m lacking in as a romantic partner,” if it were anyone else, Phainon wouldn’t even give them the time of day. But this was Mydei, a man who’s opinion he valued greatly. He trusted that Mydei would tell him not what he wanted to hear, but what he needed to hear.

Mydei sighs, he collects all the tickets off the floor, and dumps them into Phainon’s lap.

“Let’s get out of here first, this isn’t the place for a conversation.”

Whenever they go to arcades, Mydei always lets Phainon pick the prize. He says it’s because he doesn’t care about silly collectibles, but Phainon knows he has a soft spot for cute things.

“Deliverer, you didn’t have to get anything for me,” Mydei scoffs, the chimera keychain swinging around his finger. “I told you, you can pick the prizes.”

“But I wanted to get us something that matches!” Phainon says, holding his own next to Mydei’s. One has orange fur with big brown eyes, while the other has grey fur with blue eyes, the resemblance to the two of them was uncanny. “Look, it says your little guy’s name is Fig Stew, and mine’s Coconut Beagle.”

“A strange name,” Mydei huffs, but pockets the keychain nonetheless. Phainon feels a swell of pride, like a grumpy cat has accepted his offering.

“Going back to what you said earlier.” Mydei says quietly. “You are perfect as you are, there is nothing about yourself that needs to change.”

Phainon thinks if he were a lesser man he would have swooned at that. Such simple words spoken with such sincerity, like it was the most obvious fact in the world. There is nothing more validating than hearing that from Mydei, who doesn’t bother with empty praise. And yet, Phainon finds it hard to believe, surely someone who holds himself and others to such high standards will have some feedback for him.

Mydei, for all his virtues, is kind at heart. Perhaps kind enough to say what he thinks Phainon wants to hear.

“None of that nonsense, you don’t need to go easy on me. I really do want to find parts of myself that I can improve on.”

Mydei’s eyes soften, with the angle of his eyebrows lowered, he looks gentler, almost tender. “I’m not being dishonest, you are enough as you are now.”

Phainon’s breath hitches imperceptibly, but Mydei continues, unaware of the things he’s doing to his heart “You are charming and approachable, with an affability that allows you to befriend even the most difficult people. You’re also intelligent, even though sometimes you speak like someone who doesn’t have a brain.” His mouth twitches like he wants to smile. “You passed Professor Anaxagoras’s class with merits, something that only 3 people managed to accomplish this year.”

“Haha,” Phainon laughs, rubbing the back of his neck. Mydei’s praise makes him feel all light and bubbly, like a maiden in love. Is this what they call irresistible charm? Especially since he knows Mydei doesn’t give compliments lightly. “You flatter me, but there certainly must still be things I can work on? Hit me with that brutal honesty you’re so well-known for!”

The irritated expression is back, and Mydei clicks his tongue. It’s barely audible, and Phainon knows that this means he’s getting annoyed. But Mydei always humours him even when he’s being an idiot, and his jaw tightens as he puts thought, actual thought into the question.

“Something you can improve on?” Phainon finds himself leaning closer to listen better. “Well, your lack of self-confidence can be vexing, you’re always trying too hard to please people even at your own peril, and I suppose your sense of style could be better.”

Phainon immediately latches onto the third and final part, because changing his style is way easier than confronting his self-esteem issues and people pleasing tendencies.

“What part of my style do you dislike? Is it the pants?” They’re his favourite, purple with a dromas scale pattern. So soft and comfortable to wear.

“Yes, burn them, for starters. That yellow shirt as well. There is no universe where that colour combination looks good. The arcade attendee must have thought you were one of the children.”

“Alright… better clothes… style my hair… that reminds me, I have to burn my sheets at the frat house as well, I’ll burn them together with the pants.”

Mydei’s snorts at that, the corners of his lip turning up just a fraction. It’s enough to make him look devastatingly handsome. “You don’t have to take everything I say so seriously, deliverer. Like I said, the way you are presently is fine.”

Well, Phainon knows that, but there is still a part of him that feels he has to work hard to live up to the expectations others put on him. It is true that he’s fairly popular and well-liked, otherwise he wouldn’t have been accepted into the top fraternity in the first place. But Phainon can still do more, when Mydei is the picture of excellence, he certainly can’t fall behind.

After all, they’d been rivals since they first met.

The blistering heat of summer prickles Phainon’s skin, the sun tattoo on his neck, just freshly healed, itches in response to the sweat trickling down into the collar of his shirt. Okhema summers are a lot more humid compared to the ones in Aedes Elysia, something about the concrete jungle trapping the sun’s heat, so unlike the sprawling cornfields in his hometown, that distributed the heat like a warm blanket.

His hometown is rural, the kind where everyone knows each other by name. For the last month, Phainon getting accepted into the law program at the University of Okhema was the talk of the town. It feels burdensome sometimes, to carry the weight of everyone’s pride and expectations on his shoulders. It’s almost a relief to arrive in the bustling metropolitan of Okhema and become just a nameless face in the crowd.

He trudges up the stairs that lead to his dorm room, fifth floor, no elevator, dragging his bags with him all the while. By the time he arrives, he’s red-faced and panting, even though he’s not exactly unfit.

Behind the door of his future dorm room, he can hear the sound of someone moving around, it looked like his future roommate had already moved in. ‘Mydeimos’, the roster had said. It wasn’t a name native to Okhema, so maybe an outsider too, perhaps they can bond in that regard.

And because he was raised to be polite, Phainon takes a deep breath, checks out his hair with his front camera, puts on his best smile, and knocks before turning the doorknob.

Inside, crouched on the floor unpacking boxes, is the most beautiful man he’s ever seen.

The first thing he notices are his tattoos, strong red lines over smooth fair skin and taut muscle tracing throughout the entirety of his bare arms, up his neck, and even on his face. It was… definitely eye-catching, to put it mildly. But not in a distasteful way, on the contrary, Phainon found it captivating.

The next is his absurd body, the man is dressed in a loose tank top that accentuates his bulging shoulders, tapering to a narrow waist. Phainon’s been putting in his hours at the gym and he’s pretty proud of his own physique, but this guy is just on a different level. Maybe he worked as a fitness instructor in his spare time?

His roommate notices him, eyes the colour of molten gold meeting his gaze as Mydeimos lowers his headphones, Phainon can faintly hear heavy metal blaring from them.

“Are you my new roommate? I’m Mydeimos, first year history, you can call me Mydei.”

Unfortunately for him, Phainon did not catch any of that. He was too busy staring at his face. Soft blonde hair, fading to red at the tips, falling around straight eyebrows and sharp, almost feline-like eyes. His eyelashes were long and thick, like a girl’s. A face like that shouldn’t fit a body like his, and yet it all came together naturally for him.

The beautiful face frowns at him, and that’s when Phainon realizes he’s supposed to respond.

“Hi! I’m Phainon. You must be Mydeimos.” Nevermind if Phainon didn’t hear what he just said, he’s great at improvising.

But somehow, his cheerful fail proof greeting had Mydeimos frowning even deeper.

“Mydeimos is my government name, I prefer Mydei… I just said that.” His voice is deep and gravelly, like smoke from a flame. Phainon would find it pleasant, if he wasn’t absolutely mortified by the faux pas.

“I’m sorry!” This first interaction was not going like he hoped. Phainon desperately needed to salvage this. “I'm a first year law student by the way, I hope we can get along!”

He sticks out his hand for a handshake. He doesn’t like the way Mydei is looking at him, those amber eyes almost glow in the cheap dorm lighting, like they can see right through him.

“Mm,” He just grunts before pulling his headphones back over his ears and carrying on with his task. Phainon awkwardly withdraws his hand, grimacing at the cringe of it all.

Right… that could have gone better. Mydei isn’t the easiest guy to get along with, but he didn’t seem angry, just indifferent.

As Phainon gets to work unpacking his side of the room, he sneaks glances at what his roommate is doing. Mydei, to his surprise, is meticulous. His bedsheets are tucked in neatly, military style, without even a crease on its surface. His books are arranged along the shelf standing upright, and even his stationery is colour coded. He’s so conscientious that it’s almost… cute.

“Is that a chimera? I love those guys,” Phainon points to the exposed bookmark on Mydei’s bedside table, next to a collection of history books so thick and old they looked like they were written centuries ago. “I didn’t expect a scary looking guy like you to be into cute things. Do you know what ‘gap moe’ is?”

Mydei simply gives him a withering look, one that Phainon would become very familiar with in the weeks to come.

“I think we’d get along better if you didn’t speak.”

Despite Phainon’s wishes, he did not get along with Mydei. He initially thought Mydei was the kind of guy that would just ignore him, well, evidently he was wrong, because the guy was a total nag!

Phainon wouldn’t say he’s messy, after all he always cleans up after himself and doesn’t leave food on the bed, but as the assignments pile up and the social obligations increase, he finds himself slipping on cleanliness now and again.

“Deliverer, get your clothes off the floor before I trip on them!”

One time, one time , he had accidentally locked Mydei out of their room because he couldn’t hear his knocking over the sound of the horror movie playing through his earphones. In fact, he thought the furious knocks were coming from inside the movie!

Since then, Mydei has never let him live it down, referring to him as the name of the movie he had been watching.

“Deliverer, stop shining your desk lamp at my side of the room, I’m trying to sleep!”

It’s not his fault that Mydei keeps the schedule of an old man, going to sleep by 10PM and getting up at the ass crack of dawn to start his day. Phainon has to work in the darkness, so they’re both making some sacrifices here!

“You idiot! You almost burnt the entire dorm down! If you ever step into the kitchen again, I’ll personally rip out your spine!”

Okay, that was way too cruel of him. But then again, Phainon had woken the entire dorm up at 3am with the fire alarm when he decided he wanted to cook a midnight snack. Mydei, who tended to sleep shirtless, had to deal with shivering in the cold night wind while they waited for the fire department to give them the all clear.

If Phainon drapes his jacket to cover Mydei’s shirtless torso it was because he felt guilty and definitely not because of the thinly veiled lustful glances his roommate was receiving from the other students.

“Cyreneeee…. He’s the worst.” He whines to his best friend over the phone. Cyrene was three years older than him and when she left Aedes Elysia to travel the world, it gave him inspiration to move out as well.

He missed her, she was like an older sister to him, but luckily they still kept in touch over the phone.

All that goodwill evaporates when Cyrene giggles at him, she giggles! Is there anybody who feels sorry for poor Phainon’s predicament?

“I don’t think he sounds that bad. You told me that since he banned you from entering the kitchen, he’s started making your meals.”

“But he’s been making them bad on purpose! I swear he ‘accidentally’ burnt my toast this morning but his? Perfectly crisp and toasted!”

“Aww! He sounds really cute!”

“Whose side are you on?” Phainon squawks indignantly, sitting up in his bed. He runs a hand through his hair, sighing. “He’s the first person I can’t seem to make like me, no matter what I do. In fact, the harder I try the more it seems to piss him off.”

In Aedes Elysia, he was the golden boy without even trying. Now in Okhema Phainon is extremely well-liked, becoming friends with most of his coursemates within a week. Even the extremely difficult professors were starting to warm up to him. Truly, there was nobody who made Phainon feel as inadequate as Mydei, and he didn’t even have to do anything but exist.

What did he have to do to make Mydei like him?

“Why does he have to like you?” Cyrene asks, delivering armour piercing questions as casually as commenting on the weather. “You’ve been disliked by people before Phainon, it’s no big deal.”

Phainon is stunned into speechlessness, truth be told, he doesn’t even know why he’s so desperate for Mydei’s approval. Phainon was so used to being adored, so used to getting everything he wanted that he couldn’t accept having to work for someone’s approval, especially from someone whom he considered an equal.

“I mean we are roommates, after all, it’s good to get along,” he says with a weak laugh, which probably sounded unconvincing to Cyrene.

“Right, roommates .” He did not like Cyrene’s tone when she said that. “But to me, it doesn’t sound like he dislikes you at all. I wouldn’t bother nagging or making food for someone I didn’t like. Perhaps you two just need to talk it out, have a conversation.”

Phainon can only imagine how disastrous a conversation between them would go. He still can’t seem to talk to Mydei without putting his entire foot in his mouth.

Yet it’s weird, there’s something about Mydei that just draws Phainon to him, he can’t stay away.

Phainon’s gym time is one of the most treasured parts of his day. He tends to have a little too much energy at the end of a busy day and the gym is a great place to wind down until he’s too tired to overthink.

While he knows his roommate frequents the gym as well—there’s no way he could get an absurd body like that without training like crazy—their gym schedules are rarely aligned. Mydei wakes up bright and early to train before he starts his day, while Phainon tends to go in the evening and stay until he is tired.

“Oh.” Phainon says as he meets Mydei in the gym, hogging the weightlifting bench. “When you’re done can I use the bench?”

Mydei nods “I’ll be done soon,”

Phainon takes a seat next to him and watches as Mydei finishes his reps. Despite being some of the heaviest plates the gym has to offer, he’s lifting them with perfect form as though they’re weightless. If not for the bulging of his muscles and the sweat dripping down his forehead, one could think that Mydei was hardly putting in any effort at all.

“370.” Phainon says suddenly.

Mydei looks at him like he’s grown an extra head.

“What?” He asks flatly, wiping off with a gym towel. Phainon tries hard not to stare at the trail of sweat dripping past his tank top and rolling onto his tattoos.

“That’s my record, 370 lbs.” It’s a number that Phainon’s very proud of, not to brag, but he can outlift most professional athletes.

He waits for Mydei’s response, maybe to scoff and call his bluff, in which case Phainon gets to show off his impressive strength, or his jaw might drop in surprise, that’ll be fun to see.

Instead, Mydei’s lip curls up in a cat-like smirk, it’s the first time he sees him looking almost… playful and Phainon is starstruck by the sight.

“You’ll need to try harder than that, Deliverer,” Mydei says, patting the weight plates he was lifting earlier. Phainon counts and sure enough, it’s 380 lbs. It broke Phainon’s record weight and Mydei was lifting it with almost no effort.

It is Phainon’s own jaw that drops open. “You sure you’re not like, some kind of demigod or something?”

“Hmph,” Mydei snorts, but his expression is still faintly amused. “...Deadlift?”

“Excellent work today,” Aglaea says, turning around to face him. “This should be the last outfit of the day and we’re done. Consider your debt repaid.”

“I was really worried when Aglaea said she was using her godson for free labour, but you’re a real heartthrob. And that gloomy, bad-boy demeanor is an absolute ladykiller. You’re gonna go far, kid.” The photographer slinks up to him, cat-like blue eyes assessing him up and down. “Pst, if law school doesn’t work out and you want a modelling gig that’s actually paid. Feel free to keep in touch.” She slips a name card into his shirt pocket.

“Cifera,” Aglaea says in a warning tone. “Are you trying to poach my godson?”

“No ma’am!” Cipher says, winking to the very confused Phainon.

The shoot goes smoothly just like the rest of the sessions, with Phainon mostly standing there and performing a few poses when instructed by Aglaea. She seems to be pleased with the outcome, nodding after only less than half an hour.

“I think we’ve got all the shots we need. You’re free to go, Phainon, we’ll take care of the rest from here.”

Phainon looks at his phone, it’s not even 10PM.

“Yes, I told you it would last till midnight, but it looks like we’re done earlier than expected, thanks to your efficiency today.” Aglaea walks up to him, smiling softly like she just read his mind. “Any Saturday night plans?”

Phainon’s shoulders slump over. “No…”

“Pardon me for prying, but I don’t suppose you had a fight with Mydei?” Aglaea asks with an amused lilt, hand on her chin.

Phainon starts, how would she even know that? “Huh? No!”

Aglaea smiles, patting him on the shoulders like he’s a little kid. “Just a lucky guess. He’s the only one who could put you in such a bad mood. Of course, you ended up taking excellent photos, but as your godmother, I don’t like seeing you so upset. You look best when you’re smiling.”

Phainon does appreciate her attempt to cheer him up, but how can she understand the magnitude of his fumble? He smiles weakly at her. “Thanks, Aglaea, I’ll keep that in mind.”

“A real smile, not this fake one you’ve been showing us all evening,” Aglaea grips his cheeks in her hand, forcing Phainon to make a funny face like a pufferfish. “Whatever it is, I'm sure you can talk it out with Mydeimos. He’s a very nice boy and would be more than willing to hear you out.”

“B-but,” Phainon says, voice coming out distorted from his puckered lips. “What if he doesn’t feel the same way?”

“You are so called ‘best friends’, aren’t you? If he is the right one, he’ll accept you as you are.”

Phainon’s clouded gaze begins to clear, like storm clouds parting after the rain. The shimmer in his eyes returns, the dark expression replaced by something cautiously hopeful.

“I guess I won’t know if I don’t try. Thank you Aglaea, I just remembered that I did have Saturday night plans after all.”

Aglaea nods. “If you head outside, you’ll find a taxi. It was supposed to be your ride home, but if you have somewhere else to be…”

Phainon nods, just about to run off before he pauses in his tracks. “Aglaea… this outfit… can I take it with me?”

“Of course,” Aglaea smiles. “I was planning to give it to you anyway. It looks good on you.”

“Thank you once again, Aglaea!” Phainon gives a hasty wave, sprinting off in the direction of the exit.

“Oh my, working with young people is so invigorating,” Cipher sighs, placing her chin in her palm. “Reminds me of myself when I was a little kitten.”

“This is who he’s talking about, by the way,” Aglaea hides her coy smile behind her hand as she shows Cipher Mydei’s profile picture.

“WOW!” The photographer exclaims, eyes widening to the size of dinner plates. “I’ll give you your godson back if you let me poach his little boyfriend instead.”

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Mydei
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

“So…” Hephaestion tilts his head “Can we talk about the big white puppy from yesterday?” He asks, breaking the ice with all the subtlety of a sledgehammer. “Both of you acted super weird, he looked like he wanted to kill me if I breathed at him wrong, and you were trying too hard to pretend that it’s a normal thing for him to do.”

That wasn’t his fault! It was Phainon’s fault for acting weird. “I… so…” he desperately tries to change the subject. “I guess my matchmaking failed?”

Hephaestion blinks at him incredulously. Once, then twice. “Excuse me?” He says. “That was you matchmaking? Matchmaking me with who? My future murderer?”

Chapter Notes

There is no word for love in the Kremnoan dictionary. But that’s not to say that Kremnoan people don’t feel love.

To Mydei, love is a quiet thing. Love does not demand attention, love does not try to possess, love does not require reciprocation.

Love is the way his mother buys extra pomegranates when she goes to the market, knowing they’re his favourite. Love is her calloused hands holding his as she teaches him how to strum a guitar. Love is when he makes sure there’s a warm meal on the table after she comes home from a long day at work.

He is not sure when he fell in love with Phainon.

It was a slow process. At first Mydei cooks for him because he is a danger to himself and others in the kitchen, besides, he was used to shopping and cooking for two. With time he finds himself inexplicably charmed by the boyish grin that Phainon gives him whenever he eats something he particularly enjoys. Mydei becomes comfortable with how observant Phainon is, able to somehow notice when he’s having a bad day - or when that scumbag he calls a father gets ahold of his phone number again, and proposes some stupid competition to take his mind off the situation. He respects how he effortlessly navigates social situations with a smile and a laugh, pulling people to his side like a force of gravity. Phainon is handsome too, fluffy hair, sparkling blue eyes like the sky, and a sunny grin that never seems to falter no matter the situation.

A guy like Phainon effortlessly integrates into college life, becoming friends with nearly everyone regardless of background. Meanwhile Mydei… he’s quite used to being disliked, used to hushed whispers when he passes by, and used to glances that flick away the moment he meets their eye. Unfortunately, the Kremnoans still have a reputation for being ruthless brutes, and he’s sure his appearance doesn’t help. But as long as the few he holds close to his heart know the real Mydeimos, the opinions of irrelevant people don’t matter to him. Mydei shields himself with this like armour, and walks with his head held high.

And yet, this idiot …

Mydei ducks behind the wall, hiding himself from view as he listens to Phainon tear a couple of 2nd years from the business course a new one because they were talking shit about Mydei without having even spoken to him before. He can’t hear what Phainon is saying, it’s all muffled, but it is loud, and it is bold to the point that students are turning around to stare. It’s embarrassing for him and Mydei wants to tell him to stop. He doesn’t need anyone to defend him, doesn’t want anyone to. But yet a traitorous warmth blooms inside his chest, an unfamiliar, terrifying feeling that Mydei doesn’t want to acknowledge just yet.

But Phainon is the campus’ golden boy, beloved by everyone, they don’t even get along and he’s sure most people would think that Phainon is out of his league. Defending Mydei is detrimental to Phainon’s good reputation

and there’s really no benefit to it at all. Maybe if he at least bragged about it to Mydei at home then he’d understand that his motive was to get into Mydei’s good graces or at least have him indebted to Phainon. But no, that isn’t the case at all. Phainon never brings it up, it’s like it didn’t even happen.

It’s too late, the seed has already been planted in Mydei’s heart. Things that he never expected to feel, things like hope , things like want .

Kind of pathetic, falling in love with the first person he meets at college. But it is what it is.

It’s okay that Phainon does not love him back.

And when Phainon, smiling and looking at him with those gigantic puppy eyes, leans over the table and begs “Pleasseeee Mydei! Help me out! I really want to start dating!” Completely oblivious to the candidate that’s sitting right in front of him, Mydei has no choice but to agree, even though it feels like his heart is being gouged out with a fork. Because love is quiet devotion, love gives and it does not ask for reciprocation, love is invisible sacrifices.

But Mydei is just a man, he has his limits too. When Phainon tells him, with that infuriating smile, no thoughts head empty, that his type is “Someone like you, maybe? But not you, of course.” something inside him cracks.

The thought plays inside his head round and round like an infinite loop. Why not Mydei? How can Phainon describe his ideal partner and then overlook the very single Mydei that is in front of him. It eats at him like a parasite that doesn’t want to let go, and while Mydei plays it off casually, he realizes that he’s not as invulnerable as he thinks.

For the sake of his sanity, Mydei has to take a break and get his thoughts together. It starts with small things, changing his gym hours so they won’t overlap, making (rather flimsy) excuses to decline his invitations to hang out, even taking the long way around to campus so that he doesn’t

accidentally run into him. It is cowardly. Utterly shameful. He is a Kremnoan raised with courage and pride, one who should face his problems head on and not slink away like a dog with its tail between its legs. But the shame is more tolerable than the bitter ache he feels when he thinks about Phainon right now.

And perhaps Mydei is just stupid because after all of this he still wants Phainon to be happy. When his childhood friend Hephaestion gets in contact with him because he’s in Okhema for a week on a research trip, Mydei immediately thinks that perhaps he could set them up. Hephaestion is similar to Mydei in many ways, they are both stubborn, headstrong, resilient like weeds, perhaps that is why they became such good friends. Yet Hephaestion is gentle in ways that Mydei is not, soft curves where Mydei is hard muscle, like Mydei, yet not like him.

It feels like Mydei is repeatedly sticking his own hand into the claw trap, and then doing it again before the injuries can heal. But it feels right for them to meet each other, the two people Mydei considered his closest friends may fall in love with each other. Wouldn’t that be beautiful?

And as long as the people he loves are happy, Mydei could be happy too, eventually.

Yeah, no, fuck .

If Mydei could travel back in time, he’d strangle himself from a few days ago. Why did he think this was a good idea, again?

Actually, he’d go even further and stop himself from accepting Aglaea’s invitation to take Phainon clothes shopping in the first place.

What business does Phainon have showing up at his doorstep dressed like that ?

It’s annoying how good he looks in the white shirt that tightens around his broad shoulders and tapers at his narrow waist. The collar opening just

enough to be sinful but not overly scandalous. Half tucked into black jeans, it strikes the perfect balance between casual and deliberate. It’s the same with his hair, half of it pushed back, the other half left to fall in soft waves over his brow and cheekbones. Trying, but not too hard. Messy, but intentionally so.

Unfairly handsome, 100 percent.

And then there was the worst (best) part of it all, the choker, the strip of dark leather against his slender neck. It stands out against his pale skin, draws attention to his jaw, the elegant slope of his throat. The sun tattoo, its light yellow normally camouflaged against his skin, is all the more visible from underneath it. It’s like a temptation, waiting for Mydei to grab the choker like a leash and pull, to see what’s underneath.

“Do… do I look okay?” Phainon asks, shyer than usual. Mydei realizes he’s been staring too long.

“You look nice.” Mydei just says, like he hadn’t been caught fawning.

Mydei can’t help but think that if Phainon dressed like this all the time, he’d be dangerous. The boy who would become the object of every foolish crush on campus. The kind of male lead in romance novels that would have his own dedicated fanclub. Hell, even Mydei’s heart would have skipped a beat.

Is that so surprising, though? He literally picked the clothes based on what he would personally find attractive.

So this was all his fault, he’s got nobody to blame but himself. He should have just let Phainon keep wearing that stupid neon yellow t-shirt and purple dromas printed pants. Mydei has made his bed and now has to lie in it.

“Phainon, this is Hephaestion.” Mydei sees him almost missing the cue to shake Hephaestion’s hand and wonders if the latter has really got him that flustered.

His worries that his two best friends won’t get along dissipate as things dissolve into friendly banter.

“His highness speaks a lot about you.”

“His highness?”

“Oh, it’s just a nickname we used to call him in high school. It sort of stuck.”

They both turn to grin at him, Mydei rolls his eyes in response. It is a bit of a silly nickname, but he doesn’t mind it too much. It reminds him of his schooling days, of simpler times.

Mydei hears Phainon laugh, loud and forced, and hopes that he’s not misunderstanding. Him and Hephaestion are just friends, extremely close friends yes, like brothers, almost, but nothing more.

“And how long have you known Mydei?”

Hephaestion throws an arm around Mydei’s shoulder. He scowls, having half a mind to shrug him off, but he seems to attract human blankets because the last time he remembers, all his friends are this touchy. He hasn’t told Hephaestion about his intention to set him up with Phainon, which does make Mydei feel a little bad. But he’s hoping to have things develop organically between them.

“Hephaestion is pursuing his studies in anthropology, and is in town this week on a study trip curating artifacts at the museum.” Mydei explains, watching Phainon closely for the glint in his eyes that will indicate his interest. “Given your… hobbies in antiques, I thought you might get along.”

There, he’s done his part in lighting the first spark. Phainon smiles in response, but it’s the kind of smile he gives to strangers. Tight, controlled, almost fake. It’s very different from his real smile, the one he shows to Mydei.

“It’s surprising that Mydei hasn’t mentioned you to me.”

“ HKS !” Mydei exclaims in rage before he can think. It’s true that he doesn’t talk an awful lot about his life in Kremnos, but that was because his childhood held rather unpleasant memories for him. He’s definitely mentioned Hephaestion and his other friends at least once or twice. What is this HKS doing?

“No worries, I think it’s cute.” Hephaestion says cheerfully, and Mydei internally sighs in relief. Despite this disaster of a man, Hephaestion is taking it all in stride. He truly is much more patient than Mydei could ever be.

Dinner is quieter than he’s used to. With the yapper named Phainon on his right and the chatterbox named Hephaestion on his left, Mydei expected a livelier affair. He stays silent throughout most of the meal unless being directly addressed, this was a chance for Phainon and Hephaestion to get to know each other. Mydei can’t help but wonder if he had gone wrong somewhere, whether he should have informed Phainon that he was trying to set him up, first.

“What do you think about Hephaestion?” Mydei takes the opportunity to question him as Phainon still insists on helping with the cleaning, even though he’s technically a guest here. But Mydei of all people knows that the more you try to say no to him, the more you won’t be able to, so he just allows Phainon to do what he wants.

“He’s nice,” Phainon says. “I like him.”

Mydei nods, taking the words at face value. Good, great , that is a wonderful thing! That is the sound of Mydei accomplishing his goal this evening. That is the sound of victory. He should be smug as hell.

But the lump in his throat, like someone is squeezing his windpipe. The ache in his chest and the coiling unease in his gut. This is not what victory feels like.

Mydei turns away from Phainon to put away the dishes, it’s a convenient way to gather his thoughts and control his facial expressions before Phainon sees something he shouldn’t.

“If you want his number, let me know. I’m sure he won’t mind.” The offer leaves his throat unwillingly like it’s being ripped out of him but there, he’s done it. That should be more than enough intervention on his end.

Mydei leaves nature to run its course, distracting himself with preparing snacks for the movie. When he returns to the living room he finds Phainon and Hephaestion, sitting together on the couch, shoulders brushing, almost touching. They’re whispering something too, heads leaning close to each other, the ghost of a smirk on Hephaestion’s face that usually indicates he’s up to something no good.

“In my own home,” he sighs, resigning that he’s going to have to sit on the floor this evening.

The movie is… fine, kind of cliched, a little boring. Mydei usually finds it a challenge to stay awake during these things, but often forces himself through it for the sake of his friends. This time though, when his eyes flutter shut halfway through a jump scare, Mydei makes no effort to fight it. Horror movies are ripe conditions for cuddling and getting closer to someone, right? Maybe Phainon and Hephaestion can get even closer if there’s no third wheel present. Coincidentally, Mydei won’t be able to see it either, which is a plus in his eyes.

When Mydei comes to, all bleary and groggy eyed and confused, the movie is already over. His neck aches from his awkward sleeping position, and he runs his fingers through his hair to smoothen it, to little success.

“Huh, it’s over?” He mumbles intelligently, still half-asleep.

Phainon is next to him, watching him closely. He does not allow himself to startle, but Mydei does blink at him, slowly, like a cat.

“Your braid is undone,” Phainon says, in a tone that sounds too intimate for their current situation. “Let me help you with that.” He reaches forward,

closing the distance between them, intending to wrap his fingers in Mydei’s golden strands like he has done so many times before.

Except this time, a voice screams in Mydei’s head. Too close !

Acting on instinct, Mydei jerks his head back to create distance between them, stopping right before he slams his neck into the armrest. His heart is racing, his face feels hot, he can only pray that none of those things are visible to Phainon.

“Thanks, I got it,” He stands, walks, flees, into the bathroom before Phainon can say another word, getting up so quickly he makes himself dizzy in the process.

In the safety of his bathroom, Mydei leans against the sink and takes a few deep breaths before he feels like himself again. No doubt Hephaestion is going to explain his strange behaviour to Phainon, and the cat’s out of the bag. Hair is sacred to a Kremnoan, only family members or someone very close, like a partner, can touch it. His mother had carefully braided his hair as a sign of her love, and combing each other’s hair was a courting ritual according to ancient Kremnoan customs. As a historian he knows this and still, he lets Phainon touch his hair like an idiot.

Mydei knows he shouldn’t have allowed it, knows that it means more to Mydei than it does to Phainon. But he likes the feeling of Phainon’s clumsy fingers in his hair, the way the strands get tangled in his fingers and he has a tug a little to free them. He likes it when Phainon’s short fingernails scratch at his scalp. He even likes the wonky excuse of a braid he had ended up with. And in the middle of the night, when he’s all alone, Mydei can admit that he likes pretending they are something more than just friends.

Titans strike him down, he is a pathetic excuse of a Kremnoan. Mydei isn’t really sure how he will move past this embarrassment but he is going to try. He splashes his face with some cold water, carefully braids his hair into his usual style, and then goes back out to pretend like nothing’s happened.

The next morning, Mydei oversleeps. He stumbles out of his bedroom, sloppy and in a rush, only to find that breakfast has been set up for him.

“Good morning, sleepyhead.” Hephaestion says, smiling slightly. Mydei blinks at him for a moment before it comes back to him that he has a guest staying over.

“Morning, uhm, thanks.” He says, digging into the eggs and sausages that have been prepared for him. Hephaestion’s food has a certain Kremnoan style home-cooking quality that has Mydei a little nostalgic.

“It tastes like my mother’s cooking.” Gorgo, notoriously, was not a very good cook. But she made all her dishes with love, so Mydei eats it all up anyway.

“That my friend, I’ll take as a compliment.” Hephaestion pats him on the back. “It’s unlike you to oversleep, by the way. I think you already missed your first class so you might as well not go in at all. I think your attendance can take a hit.”

Mydei sighs, it can, but he’s not the type to skip class, much less oversleep.

“So…” Hephaestion tilts his head “Can we talk about the big white puppy from yesterday?” He asks, breaking the ice with all the subtlety of a sledgehammer. “Both of you acted super weird, he looked like he wanted to kill me if I breathed at him wrong, and you were trying too hard to pretend that it’s a normal thing for him to do.”

That wasn’t his fault! It was Phainon’s fault for acting weird. “I… so…” he desperately tries to change the subject. “I guess my matchmaking failed?”

Hephaestion blinks at him incredulously. Once, then twice. “Excuse me?” He says. “That was you matchmaking ? Matchmaking me with who? My future murderer?”

“Surely you exaggerate.” Mydei rolls his eyes.

“That’s because his eyes fill with stars the moment you look his way.” Hephaestion grumbles under his breath. “It must be a skill to misread a situation so spectacularly.”

“You did not see the look on his face when he found out I was sleeping over here,” Hephaestion says out loud instead. “I saw my life flash before my eyes.”

Mydei frowns, as though that was a completely new discovery for him. “That’s a shame…” Mydei says quietly. “I hoped you two would get along as my best friends.”

“Oh, I’m sure we’d get along just fine once he sees I’m not a threat.”

“A threat to what?” Mydei frowns, his eyes immediately roving across Hephaestion’s slender frame and skinny arms. He doubted Hephaestion could match either of them in physical strength. Hephaestion hugs himself, immediately offended by the insinuation.

“Oh sweet Mydeimos, you can’t possibly be this daft.” Hephaestion looks torn on whether to slap Mydei or to slap himself. “Let me just spell it out plainly for you, Phainon was staring at you the whole evening.”

Mydei crosses his arms over his chest stubbornly. “I did not notice that.”

“Oh trust me, he did not like to share. You’ve snatched up quite the possessive little doggy.”

“...He can be quite dog-like, now that you mentioned it.” Mydei muses almost fondly.

Hephaestion looks like he wanted to rip his hair out, surely that cannot be the only thing he takes away from this conversation.

“But anyway, you’re mistaken.” Mydei continues, oblivious to the torment he is putting Hephaestion through. “He doesn’t like me that way, we’ve talked about it.”

“You have?” Hephaestion raises a disbelieving eyebrow. “And did he explicitly use the words ‘I have no romantic inclinations towards you, Mydeimos of Castrum Kremnos.’ in that order?”

“...Not exactly, but the message was clear enough. He said that I was his type, but not me. That was why I tried to introduce him to you.”

“Ah.” Hephaestion says, pauses, nods like he just received the answer to a particularly perplexing puzzle. “I understand the situation now.”

Mydei gives him a look, unconvinced, Hephaestion only smiles at him. “If I tell you that I think you’re wrong, and that Phainon is down abysmal for you, would you believe me?”

“No. You’ve been making statements like that for years and it’s never been true.”

“On the contrary,” Hephaestion whispers under his breath. “It’s always been true and you are just wrong.”

But on the outside he smiles wider. “Mydeimos, may I request a favour.”

Mydei looks suspicious about this sudden change in topic, sentences that start with ‘Mydeimos’ rarely end with anything good. But he’s somewhat relieved at the change in subject anyway. “Ask.”

“This weekend coincides with a public holiday in Kremnos. I’ve decided I want to try Okheman clubbing.”

“Go by yourself.” Mydei replies immediately.

Hephaestion gasps like he’s been struck “Mydeimos! You said you would grant me a favour.” he sulks. “Come on, it’ll be fun! We’ll invite all the old gang, Leonnius, Ptolemy, Perdikkas, Peucesta, it’ll be our reunion!”

“A reunion? At a nightclub?” Mydei repeats, disdain dripping from every word.

“Do invite Phainon as well,” Hephaestion says, completely steamrolling over Mydei.

Mydei blinks. “Clubbing isn’t his thing either.”

“Trust me, if you’re there. He’ll come. Come on, I’ll handle the invitations, the bookings, all of it. You just invite him.” Hephaestion says insistently.

Mydei isn’t sure what plan he has cooking up this time. Hephaestion has always been like that, sly, cheeky, a real trickster. But one thing is true, once he makes up his mind, he’ll stop at nothing to bug Mydei until he gets his way.

Come to think of it, he and Phainon are extremely similar, in that regard. Had he misread things so badly? Would they really not like each other? But they have so much in common, whilst Mydei and Phainon are like polar opposites.

“Fine.” Mydei sighs, regretting his life choices. “I’ll ask him.”

“Great,” Hephaestion says, he doesn’t rub his hands with glee, but he might as well have.

The pulsing of the strobe lights and the loud thumping of the bass worsens Mydei’s headache and reminds him why he can’t stand nightclubs. The place is crowded already, sweaty bodies grinding against each other, drinks being chugged and spilled on the floor, the air smelling like cheap perfume.

It’s been ages since he’s last seen his old friends, and although Mydei is happy to be reunited again, he wished it was under better conditions. He can’t even speak to them without shouting over the music. Somehow Leonnius is already drunk, spinning around the dance floor with Hephaestion having the time of their lives.

Mydei leans against the seat of his booth, legs spread in a languid sprawl, drink in hand. Pomegranate juice with milk, his favourite, a wonder this

place even sells it.

He dressed up for the occasion, Hephaestion had insisted. A scarlet tailored shirt with intricate gold patterns that practically clings to his shoulders, sleeves rolled up to reveal bare forearms, tucked loosely into fitted black pants. The top buttons are undone, revealing the tight black turtleneck he is wearing underneath, stretched tight over his collarbones like a second skin. A golden chain hangs around his neck, catching the light, and dramatic earrings with sapphires embedded in them glint from his ears. They are gifts from his mother, a relic of Kremnoan culture. While normally a bit too flashy for his daily style, it works perfectly with what he’s wearing tonight. Even his hair is done up nicely, top half braided from both temples, meeting in a half ponytail fixed with a blood red gem.

He looks pretty good. It’s definitely more of an effort than he usually makes to go out.

Too bad Phainon isn’t here to see it.

He did understand why. Aglaea’s modelling job was infinitely more important, especially when he owed her. Plus, Mydei can’t say he was jumping for joy at the idea of watching Phainon get flirted with all evening by random strangers. Assuming that he’s still actively looking for a partner. So perhaps this was for the best.

That HKS needs to take better care of himself anyway. He was acting weird last weekend at dinner, then he acted even weirder when he was sick. Mydei can’t make heads nor tails of his recent behavior.

“Careful,” Hephaestion says, suddenly beside him, cheeks flushed with exertion. “If you keep brooding like that you’re going to have half the club falling at your feet.”

Mydei gives him a withering look. “Shut up and go back to dancing.”

“Don’t look so grumpy,” Hephaestion laughs, taking a seat beside him and putting his arm around Mydei. “Tonight is for you.”

“What?” Mydei’s ideal weekend night is staying at home reading, or baking, or playing guitar, or hanging out with Phainon.

Huh, he wonders when that made the list of his ideal weekend plans?

“I want you to forget about Phainon for a moment.” Hephaestion’s accusation feels like a slap in the face, considering that he actually had been thinking of him.

“I’m not thinking about him,” Mydei lies.

“Liar. You look hot as hell, too hot to waste just sitting here. Go on the dance floor, have fun, meet someone pretty.”

“I think I’m fine,” Mydei rolls his eyes. Unlike Phainon, he doesn’t care for a quick hookup. He’s quite happy being single.

“Alright, then at least go get us some drinks. We’re running out and you know how prickly Perdikkas is when he doesn’t have anything to mix.”

He nudges Perdikkas, who simply nods in agreement. “I’m about to start mixing the peanuts.” He says with a straight face.

Mydei huffs. “Alright,” At least it gives him something to do.

Mydei grumbles as he pushes through the dancing crowd, making apologies when necessary. It’s impossible not to make contact with other people in a place as dense as this, but some of these touches don’t feel accidental.
